Amazon Fashion · Generative AI · 2023

Generative AI Fashion Shopping

A generative AI fashion shopping concept where customers design what they can't find the words for, and shopping happens as a byproduct of creating, built before the industry had a name for it.

Role · Design vision lead, PRFAQ to MLP
Presented to · L10 leadership
Status · Predated Google, Pinterest, and the 2024 generative AI retail wave

The problem

Customers are overwhelmed by Amazon's selection and can't find the words to describe what they want. 21% of broad fashion searches are abandoned. 66% of customers wish they could find further variations of a color or print after using visual search. They turn to social media instead of completing their mission on Amazon.

The insight: what if the gap between imagination and purchase could be closed by letting customers design what they want, then shop what emerges?

Research that shaped the design

The CX was grounded in primary research on what makes shopping fun, a diary study across six categories of intrinsic motivator.

Creative experiences

Ranked highest for fashion. Fun came from using imagination, browsing inspiration, mentally planning outfits, and personalizing or customizing.

Achievement

Fun when finally finding the "right" item, especially after a hunt. Sorting and filtering by what matters, and efficient comparison, helped.

Browsing inspiration

Prominent imagery, photos and video, plus ways to save and categorize content like lists and boards, drove creative engagement.

Customization as delight

Customers described fun when making decisions that resulted in personalized products, choosing exact colors, fabrics, and materials.

A fifth thread ran through all of it: for Gen Z, everyone is a creator. The emerging consumer mindset is participatory, not passive, customers want tools for self-expression, not just consumption. Together, these insights pointed to one design direction: creative tools that naturally lead to product discovery. Not a conventional search bar, not a chatbot, but a new entry point into search and discovery, one where imagination becomes the query.

The PRFAQ vision: what was designed

The PRFAQ was brought to life through design in a highly ambiguous space where product wasn't always defined. The end-to-end CX:

01

Personalized starting points

No blank canvas. Customers begin with personalized outfit recommendations or an uploaded inspiration image.

02

AI-generated designs

The experience generates full outfits based on the initial prompt, what the customer envisions but can't find in the catalog.

03

Multi-modal refinement

Text prompts ("longer sleeves"), uploaded reference images, or tapping an element from another product. Three input modes for three ways of thinking.

04

Discovery as a byproduct

Every generated design surfaces visually similar purchasable products automatically. The customer never has to search, they create, and shopping follows.

05

Element combination

Select a detail from one product and apply it to another, the neckline of this dress with the print of that one.

06

Boards as memory

Save designs into themed collections. The AI uses board context to inform future sessions, context compounds over time.

07

Integration across the store

It lives within the existing shopping journey, not as a standalone destination, with ingresses from Search (89M queries/yr), Detail Page, Amazon Discover, and Amazon Lens, each contextualizing the experience differently.

Key design decisions

Visual-first input over text-first

Unlike chatbots that start with a text prompt, this starts with visual inspiration. Removes the blank-page problem, fashion intent is visual, not verbal.

Progressive refinement over one-shot generation

Each generation is a conversation, not a query, mirroring how people actually think about fashion: "I like this but different."

Creation IS discovery

Product discovery happens automatically as a byproduct of designing. The customer never switches modes from creating to shopping.

Inclusive by design

Diverse skin tone, size, and body type representation in all generated content. Avatar customization as self-expression, not cosmetic.

What happened

After the initial PRFAQ review, leadership directed a pivot toward gamification, leaderboards, challenges, hearts, to make the CX more simple and fun. The gamified MLP was designed while preserving the core design-to-discover insight underneath. From a design perspective, the original browse and discovery framing was the stronger CX, and the research backed it: customers described fun during creative experiences that led to shopping outcomes, not competition for its own sake.

Design was ultimately taken as far as it could go. The blocker was the AI-generated imagery. Months of iteration with the science team couldn't get content quality to a bar ready for beta launch, only 0.1% of generated images passed Shop by Interest curation. Model defects, contextualization issues, and ASIN similarity matching all remained unsolved when the charter changed in late 2023.

Legacy

2023

Direct lineage to Solemate. The PRFAQ design principles, visual-first, progressive AI refinement, intent-over-attributes, creation-as-search, multi-modal input, became Solemate's foundation 18 months later, which shipped to production. Notably, Solemate used the original browse and discovery framing, not the gamified pivot.

2023–25

Established the org's AI shopping SME role. The first project to establish this as an area of expertise, expanded through Solemate and now informing the Deals Page AI work.

2023–24

Predated industry trends. Google's virtual try-on, Pinterest's AI styling, and the broader generative AI retail wave all followed patterns this concept explored first at Amazon.

Defined the design vision for an entirely new product category in a space with no established patterns, operating at the intersection of product definition and design execution, making decisions that shaped what the product was, not just how it looked. The thinking established here directly enabled Solemate's 30-day sprint to production 18 months later.
